1 What was extracted, and from what

1716 model calls over 260 records completed with 0 failures. Nineteen fields were extracted in three schema-constrained groups; the remaining seven of the protocol’s twenty-six are bibliographic and were carried from OpenAlex metadata rather than re-read off the page, because asking a model to restate a field we already hold exactly would manufacture error where ground truth exists.

eb <- ext |> dplyr::distinct(id, evidence_base, text_source) |>
  dplyr::count(evidence_base, text_source)
knitr::kable(eb, caption = "What text each record was extracted from")
What text each record was extracted from
evidence_base text_source n
full_text full_body_fallback 4
full_text full_body_fallback_truncated 13
full_text methods_results 95
full_text methods_results_truncated 4
title_abstract title_abstract 144

Records with retrievable full text were extracted from the methods and results sections of the GROBID TEI; the rest from title and abstract. Extracting only from full text would have redefined the map as a map of the open-access subset, which Module 05 showed is not drawn evenly across countries. Every value carries its evidence_base, and the reliability figures below are stratified by it.

2 The four verification mechanisms

2.1 1. Quote-grounding — a directly measured hallucination rate

Every non-null value carries a verbatim quote, string-matched back against the source text after normalising whitespace, case and quotation glyphs. A quote that cannot be found sets the value to NA with reason unverified_quote.

g <- ext |> dplyr::filter(is_positive) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(),
                   grounded = sum(grounded_main %in% TRUE),
                   rate = round(mean(grounded_main %in% TRUE), 4))
knitr::kable(g, caption = "Quote-grounding over positive claims")
Quote-grounding over positive claims
n grounded rate
1957 1871 0.9561

95.6% of positive claims were grounded, so the measured hallucination rate is 4.4%. That is stronger evidence than any spot-check, because it is computed over every value rather than a sample.

Two design decisions shape this number and both cut against flattering it. Quotes joined by an ellipsis are split and every segment must match, so a stitched-together citation is not scored as correct. Conversely, values that assert absence — "no", "not measured", "not stated" — are exempt, because no paper contains a sentence saying “we tested no mitigation”. Grounding measures whether asserted presence is real.

gb <- ext |> dplyr::group_by(evidence_base) |>
  dplyr::summarise(positive = sum(is_positive),
                   grounding = round(mean(grounded_main[is_positive] %in% TRUE), 4),
                   .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(gb, caption = "Grounding by evidence base")
Grounding by evidence base
evidence_base positive grounding
full_text 755 0.9470
title_abstract 1202 0.9617

Grounding is essentially identical whether the source was full text or an abstract, which is reassuring: the model is not compensating for a thinner evidence base by inventing more.

2.2 2. Self-consistency — measured, not assumed

sc <- ext |> dplyr::filter(is_stated) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(),
                   lenient = round(mean(consistent %in% TRUE), 4),
                   strict  = round(mean(consistent_strict %in% TRUE), 4))
knitr::kable(sc, caption = "Agreement between run 1 and run 2")
Agreement between run 1 and run 2
n lenient strict
2379 0.9424 0.9248

Module 04b reported self-consistency of exactly 1.0000 with zero flips across 60,000 records. That number measured nothing: temperature 0 with a fixed seed is deterministic, so identical inputs must produce identical outputs.

Here run 2 uses a different seed at temperature 0.3, so the two runs can differ, and the resulting 0.942 is an actual robustness measurement. This is a deliberate protocol deviation and is recorded as one.

Enum fields are compared exactly; free-text fields also count as agreeing when one run’s value contains the other’s (“jackal” vs “golden jackal”), since a strict string test on free text measures phrasing rather than stability. Both figures are reported — strict is 0.925.

2.3 3. Cross-model agreement

A random 20% of records were re-extracted with qwen2.5:7b, a different training lineage from gemma4:e4b.

2.4 4. “not stated” everywhere

Every enum carries the escape hatch. Without one the model invents plausible values, and absence is exactly what this map measures.

ab <- ext |> dplyr::filter(is_stated) |>
  dplyr::summarise(stated = dplyr::n(),
                   absence_assertions = sum(!is_positive),
                   pct = round(100 * mean(!is_positive), 1))
knitr::kable(ab, caption = "How often the model asserted absence rather than a value")
How often the model asserted absence rather than a value
stated absence_assertions pct
2379 422 17.7

unreliable <- rel$field[!rel$reliable %in% TRUE]

5 of 19 fields fall below the 0.7 floor and are excluded from Module 07’s headline analysis: damage_metric_reported, compensation_scheme_discussed, study_design, subnational_region, species_scientific.

binding <- rel |>
  dplyr::mutate(worst = dplyr::case_when(
    cross_model <= pmin(grounding, self_consist, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "cross-model",
    self_consist <= pmin(grounding, cross_model, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "self-consistency",
    TRUE ~ "grounding")) |>
  dplyr::count(worst, sort = TRUE)
knitr::kable(binding, caption = "Which measure is the binding constraint, per field")
Which measure is the binding constraint, per field
worst n
cross-model 16
self-consistency 3

Cross-model agreement is the binding constraint on almost every field, and by a wide margin: grounding runs 0.93-1.00 and self-consistency 0.75-1.00, while cross-model runs 0.48-0.98.

That is the honest headline of this module. A single model is internally consistent and quotes the source faithfully, and still disagrees substantially with a different model reading the same text. Verification against the source catches fabrication; it does not catch interpretation. Only a second model does, and it is what excluded five fields.

p <- rel |>
  dplyr::select(field, grounding, self_consist, cross_model) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-field, names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") |>
  dplyr::mutate(measure = dplyr::recode(measure, grounding = "quote-grounding",
                                        self_consist = "self-consistency",
                                        cross_model = "cross-model")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = reorder(field, value), colour = measure, shape = measure)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = FIELD_RELIABILITY_MIN, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = OKABE[c(6, 5, 3)]) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.3, 1.02)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL,
       title = "Per-field extraction reliability",
       subtitle = sprintf("Dashed line is the %.2f floor. Cross-model agreement binds almost everywhere.",
                          FIELD_RELIABILITY_MIN)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
print(p)

dir.create(here::here(DIR_FIGURES), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
ggsave(here::here(DIR_FIGURES, "06_field_reliability.png"), p, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
ggsave(here::here(DIR_FIGURES, "06_field_reliability.svg"), p, width = 8, height = 5)
